transcript.text: Thank you all. Let me address Ravi's recommendation first. The campaign-freeze checklist does not require an additional inspection-turnaround estimate when the released customer file does not provide one. The customer file specifies the requirement — scanning of the first 30 units before the remaining 150 can be released — but does not specify inspection location or method. Per our standard checklist, that's sufficient to record the constraint and proceed. We don't need to delay the freeze to chase down information the customer file doesn't provide. Now, here's my sequencing decision based on everything recorded: We run Order K — the 320 aluminum brackets — first, then Order L — the 180 stainless enclosures. Here's why: First, running K first means we stay in the aluminum family from the start with zero setup loss, and we only incur one material-family change when we switch to stainless for L. If we ran L first, we'd still need that same stainless setup, plus we'd incur 2 hours of downtime for Marta's regulator replacement before any part runs — and then we'd need a second setup to switch back to aluminum for K, and then a third setup to switch back to stainless if we had to revisit L. Running K first avoids that. Second, Marta can perform the 2-hour regulator replacement during the aluminum run, so L is ready to go the moment K finishes — that downtime is absorbed rather than added to the front of the campaign. Third, Jonas confirmed no shipping constraints on K, so running K first carries no logistics risk. The Friday 10:00 staging deadline for L is the binding shipping constraint, and we'll plan the full campaign to ensure all 180 enclosures are staged by that time. So to summarize the frozen plan: Sequence is K first, then L. Maintenance downtime is 2 hours for the regulator replacement, performed during the K run.
